html:
The Pacaxes were a little known Indigenous people of western Mexico, shown on the map in the foothills of the Sierra Madre Occidental where Sinaloa meets Durango, inland from the present city of Culiacán.

Almost nothing is recorded about them beyond the name. The peoples of these mountains, such as the Xiximes and Acaxees, farmed maize in the canyons and lived in small scattered settlements. From the 1590s Jesuit missionaries tried to gather them into mission towns, and revolts, epidemics and resettlement broke them up during the 1600s. The Pacaxes probably shared that fate. Their neighbours on the coast below were the Tahue.
sum: The Pacaxes were a little known Indigenous people of western Mexico, shown on the map in the foothills of the Sierra Madre Occidental where Sinaloa meets Durango, inland from the present city of Culiacán.
